title: Rigid Core vs Flexible Vinyl Plank: Which One Do You Actually Want?
meta: Rigid core vs flexible vinyl plank for Edmonds homes: rigid hides subfloor flaws and floats, flexible glues down and stays put. Wills Flooring, $2.50 per sq ft labor.
keywords: rigid core vs flexible vinyl plank, rigid core LVP vs LVT, glue down vinyl plank vs click lock, flexible luxury vinyl plank pros and cons, vinyl plank flooring Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: Most Edmonds homeowners want rigid core: it floats, it bridges small subfloor flaws, and it goes in fast. Flexible glue-down vinyl plank wins in a narrower set of rooms: very flat slabs, heavy rolling loads, and spaces where a floating floor would move.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs both at $2.50 per sq ft labor. The plank itself is where the decision, and most of the money, lives. Here is how we choose between them house by house.

blocks.html: Walk into any flooring store and you will hear "rigid core" a dozen times. It is the SPC and WPC click-lock plank that has taken over the vinyl aisle. Flexible vinyl plank, the thinner glue-down product that came first, is still made and still sold, and in Edmonds we install a fair amount of it in Bowl condos and on the slab levels of Seaview and Westgate homes. A common Reddit thread asks whether flexible is just the cheap version. It is not; it is a different tool. The vinyl plank page has our rates, and this post has the decision.

blocks.text: What the two words actually mean

items.title: Rigid core: a stiff plank that floats
items.text: A 4 to 8 mm plank with a stone-plastic (SPC) or wood-plastic (WPC) core, a vinyl print layer and a wear layer on top. Planks click together and lie loose on the subfloor with a small expansion gap at the walls. Nothing is glued.

items.title: Flexible: a thin plank that is glued
items.text: A 2 to 3 mm solid vinyl plank you can bend in your hands. It is spread with adhesive or set on a pressure-sensitive glue and pressed down. Every plank is bonded to the subfloor, so the floor cannot shift, lift or drum.

items.title: Rigid forgives, flexible telegraphs
items.text: Rigid core bridges small dips and seams in the subfloor. Flexible shows every one of them within a month: a nail head, a plywood seam, a grain of grit under the plank. It demands a flat, clean, sealed subfloor.

items.title: Both are waterproof planks
items.text: Neither swells when wet. The difference is what happens to water that gets past them. A glued floor keeps it out of the seams better; a floating floor lets a spill run underneath and sit on the subfloor.

blocks.text: How we decide at an Edmonds estimate

items.text: A 10 ft straightedge across the room. Under 3/16 in of variation and both are on the table. Over that, rigid core or a leveling pass; flexible is off unless you pay for flatness.
items.note: Seaview ramblers on plank subfloor usually fail this test

items.d: 2. What is the subfloor made of
items.text: Concrete slab in a daylight basement or Bowl condo: either works, and glue-down is our usual pick. Plywood or OSB: rigid core floats over it happily. Old particleboard: neither, until it is replaced.
items.note: Slab moisture is tested before any glue-down

items.text: A west-facing room above the water gets real afternoon sun. Floating WPC can expand and peak. Glue-down or a quality SPC stays flat.
items.note: Perrinville and the Bowl have the most of these rooms

items.text: Kitchen islands, wheelchairs, rolling chairs, a 600 lb fridge: glue-down. Ordinary furniture and foot traffic: rigid core is fine.
items.note: Retirees downsizing into Edmonds condos often plan for mobility

items.text: One long run through a kitchen, hall and great room without a doorway to hide a transition strongly favors glue-down.
items.note: Floating floors need a break every 40 to 50 ft

blocks.text: Which one for which Edmonds room

a.title: Choose it when
items: The subfloor is plywood or OSB with normal seams and nail heads
You want the job done in a day or two with no adhesive cure
Rooms are bedrooms, halls and living areas with doorways between them
You may want to lift a plank for a future repair without solvents
You are covering old vinyl or tile you do not want to remove

b.title: Choose it instead when
items: The floor is a flat, tested concrete slab
Heavy rolling loads or mobility equipment will use the room
The run is long and open with nowhere for a transition
A west or south window bakes the floor every afternoon
The room is a condo where sound transfer to the unit below matters

blocks.title: The flatness problem nobody mentions in the store:
blocks.text: Flexible plank on a 1960s Edmonds plank subfloor without a plywood overlay and a skim coat will show every board line by spring. The plank is not defective; the floor under it is uneven. If a quote for flexible glue-down has no prep line, ask how the installer plans to get the subfloor flat, because a good one cannot skip it.
Mistakes we get called to fix

items.html: Rigid core over a soft, bouncy subfloor. Rigid bridges dips, not movement. Loose subfloor sheets pop the locking joints. Screw the subfloor down first.
Flexible plank with grit under it. A single piece of drywall crumb telegraphs as a bump forever. The slab has to be vacuumed twice, then wiped.
No expansion gap on a floating floor. Base shoe nailed tight to the plank locks it in place, and it buckles at the first warm week. Gap at every wall, every cabinet, every post.

Wrong adhesive on a damp slab. Standard pressure-sensitive glue releases when slab moisture climbs. A moisture test and, if needed, a moisture-tolerant adhesive or a sealer are not optional on Edmonds slabs.

Buying by thickness alone. A 3 mm flexible plank with a 20 mil wear layer will outlast an 8 mm rigid plank with a 6 mil wear layer. Compare wear layers, not core thickness. Our post on plank thickness covers that.

blocks.text: What to ask before you buy either one

items.html: What is the wear layer in mils? 12 mil is the floor for a busy house, 20 mil for dogs and rentals, whichever core you pick.
Did you check the subfloor with a straightedge? If the answer is no, the quote is a guess about prep.
Was the slab moisture tested? Any glue-down over concrete needs a number on the quote.
Where will the transitions be? For a floating floor, ask to see them drawn on the layout before install day.

Who warranties what? The manufacturer covers the plank; Wills Flooring covers the installation for a year. Bring both samples to the house, in the room's light, before deciding. We do that at every free estimate.

faq.q: Is rigid core vinyl plank better than flexible vinyl plank?
faq.a: Better for most rooms, not all. Rigid core floats over ordinary plywood subfloors, hides small flaws and installs quickly. Flexible glue-down is better on flat concrete, under heavy rolling loads, in long open runs and in sunny rooms where a floating floor would move. Match the product to the room.

faq.q: Does flexible vinyl plank cost more to install than rigid core?
faq.a: Wills Flooring charges the same $2.50 per sq ft labor for both. Flexible usually costs more in total because it needs adhesive and a flatter subfloor, which means more prep. Those items are quoted at the free estimate after we check the floor.

faq.q: Can rigid core vinyl plank be glued down?
faq.a: Some SPC products are rated for glue-down and we do it on slabs where the owner wants a floating look with a bonded feel. Most rigid core is designed to float, and gluing a product not rated for it voids the warranty. Check the spec sheet.

faq.q: Which is quieter, rigid core or glue-down vinyl plank?
faq.a: Glue-down is quieter underfoot because there is no air gap and nothing to drum. Rigid core with a good attached pad is close. In Edmonds condos with a neighbor below, glue-down or rigid core over an acoustic underlayment approved by the HOA is the usual answer.

faq.q: Which one handles Edmonds humidity better?
faq.a: Both are waterproof planks and neither swells. Humidity affects the floating floor more because it expands and contracts as a sheet, which is why the expansion gap matters. Glue-down cannot move, so seasonal swings near the water are a non-issue for it.

faq.q: Can I install flexible vinyl plank over my existing vinyl floor?
faq.a: Sometimes, if the old sheet vinyl is fully bonded, smooth and single-layer, with an embossing leveler over the texture. Cushioned or loose vinyl has to come out. Rigid core is far more forgiving here and often goes straight over old vinyl.
